lesson.title: Data about you
lesson.subtitle: Fine to share, share with care, or keep private

video.title: Data about you
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — the class teacher (main character)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: A cat game; Name, school, birthday; And a photo. Amina beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A cat game on a phone asked Grace for her name, her school, her birthday and a photo. Just to play a game about cats!

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: data about you, and what to keep private.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Name and age; School, where you live; Photo and voice; Your marks.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Data about you is anything that tells people who you are. Your name, your age, your school, where you live. Your photo, your voice, your marks.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Fine: your favourite fruit; Care: your photo; Private: address, phone, passwords.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some data is fine to share, like your favourite fruit. Some needs care, like your photo. And some stays private: your address, your phone number and your passwords.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Your school; When you walk home; Your street.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Small facts add up. Your school, plus the time you walk home, plus your street. Together, a stranger could find you.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Which of these is fine to share with your whole class?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: What you like, not where you are
scenes.narration: Your favourite fruit: it says what you like, not where to find you. Addresses and passwords stay private.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: Stop before you type; Ask a trusted adult; You can always say no.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Before you type your details into a game, a website or an app, stop. Ask a trusted adult, like a parent or a teacher. And you can always say no.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Six posts; Together: a lot; Make her safe.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, Lina is fourteen. Her six posts look harmless, but together they tell a stranger a lot. Choose who can see each post, and make her safe.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A website says: type your home address, and win a prize! What do you do?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Your data belongs to you; Fine, care, or private; Small facts add up; Not sure? Ask an adult. Takeaway bar: Think before you share; ask when you're not sure.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Stop, and ask a trusted adult first: a prize that wants your address is often a trick. Remember: data about you belongs to you. Some is fine to share, some needs care, and some stays private. And small facts add up.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: With your family; Three boxes on paper; Ten facts, sorted. Amina beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: with your family, draw three boxes on paper: fine, care and private. Write ten facts about you, and sort them into the boxes.

checkpoints.prompt: Which of these is fine to share with your whole class?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it says what you like, not where to find you or how to get into your things.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — your address shows where to find you, and a password must stay secret. Your favourite fruit is fine to share.

checkpoints.prompt: A website says: type your home address and win a prize! What do you do?

options.text: Type it fast, before the prize is gone
Stop, and ask a trusted adult first

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — stop and ask. A prize that wants your address is often a trick.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — never rush to type your address, or someone else's. Stop, and ask a trusted adult first.
